legal_source_reads.note: The FTC page does not promise the item IS solid gold when the word is absent; the absence of the word is simply not evidence. The project's 'solid_gold_status: not_stated' treatment is consistent with this wording.

legal_source_reads.statute_title_as_printed: 15 U.S. Code § 295 - Standard of fineness of gold articles; deviation
what_the_page_says_that_the_project_reli: actual fineness shall not be less by more than three one-thousandth parts than the fineness marked (solder-free sample)
in addition, the entire article including solder shall not be less by more than three one-thousandth (watchcase/flatware) or seven one-thousandth (any other article) than the marked fineness
"it being intended that the standards of fineness and the tests or methods for ascertaining the same provided in this section ... shall be concurrent and not alternative"
legal_source_reads.arithmetic_check: 0.5833 - 0.007 = 0.5763 (14K) and 1.0 - 0.007 = 0.993 (24K) match data/methodology.json's minimum_fineness_if_stamped values 0.5763333 and 0.993, which are the figures the site's legal-minimum column uses.

derivation_audit.method: independent Decimal implementation (ROUND_HALF_UP), reading data/rings.json, data/methodology.json and data/gold_spot.json; no import of scripts/compute.py or scripts/audit.py
derivation_audit.rounding_note_detail: VRAI aggregate multiple_min/max/avg print 3.75 while exact-decimal arithmetic gives 3.76 (VR-01: 1035 USD / 275.604... USD of gold = 3.755457; at two decimals ROUND_HALF_UP is 3.76). scripts/compute.py rounds the already 3-dp value with binary float round(), which lands on 3.75. The published row-level figure 3.755 is correct; only the two-decimal presentation and the retailer aggregate are one hundredth low.
